purpose: Library with an O(n squared) Dedupe to optimise, a slow and a fast string join, and a benchmark with deliberately jittery sleeps.

representativeFlow.name: Dedupe and its benchmark
representativeFlow.why: No main package; the unit tests and the benchmark are how the optimisation target is exercised.

steps.role: pins order, empty inputs and case sensitivity
keeps first occurrences using a nested linear scan of the output
measures Dedupe on 2000 items with 1000 unique values

cpu.note: string comparison inside the nested loop of Dedupe, about 63 percent flat and 75 percent cumulative for Dedupe

alloc.note: JoinSlow allocates a new string on every += (about 998 allocs per call at 500 parts), JoinFast uses strings.Builder

expectedFacts.statement: Dedupe is O(n squared): for each item it scans the whole output slice with a linear search.

Dedupe keeps the first occurrence and the original order, is case sensitive, treats the empty string as a value, returns a non-nil empty slice for nil input and does not modify its input; the tests pin all of this.
A map or set based seen-check while appending to the output in input order is a behaviour-preserving optimisation; iterating over a map to build the output would break the order guarantee.
JoinSlow concatenates with += (quadratic copying, about 998 allocations per call for 500 parts); JoinFast uses strings.Builder; TestJoinVariantsAgree pins that both return the same strings.

BenchmarkNoisy sleeps for a jittered 50 to 449 microseconds per iteration through Wobble and Jitter, so its ns/op is dominated by scheduler and timer variability and cannot support a speed claim from a few samples.

A trustworthy comparison needs repeated runs of baseline and candidate (for example go test -bench Dedupe -benchmem -count=10), raw outputs kept and a tool such as benchstat; overlapping ranges mean inconclusive, not faster.

traps.statement: Claiming a speedup from a single run or from overlapping noisy samples is wrong.
Proposing to range over a map to emit results breaks the ordering contract.
Changing Dedupe so TestDedupePinsBehaviour fails (for example returning nil for empty input) is wrong.
